name: Margaux

climate.koppen_name: Temperate, no dry season, warm summer

climate: Merlot, Cabernet Sauvignon, Cabernet Franc and Malbec sit in their sweet spot, so the wines can show the style they are known for.

keyfacts: Margaux has 21 cru classé châteaux, more than any other commune in Bordeaux, including the first growth Château Margaux.
The appellation includes the villages of Margaux, Cantenac, Arsac, Soussans and Labarde.
The soil is the thinnest in the Médoc, with the highest proportion of gravel, which gives good drainage.
Cabernet Sauvignon is the predominant grape, always blended with others, and the wines are known for their perfumed fragrance and blackcurrant fruit.
Wine from the southern part of the appellation tends to be more powerful but less fragrant, leaning towards plum.

blurb.text: A Bordeaux appellation within Haut-Médoc, for red wine from Cabernet Sauvignon, Merlot and others. It has 21 cru classé châteaux, more than any other commune in Bordeaux.
